assumptions_resolved: The bounded read-back follows the existing --claim dispatch recovery loop in scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs rather than a new pattern, with the same injectable wait so the retries are testable without real sleeps. completeOutcome now uses that same bounded confirmation instead of the single read the pull request exists to fix.

Repair is strictly append-only: a new recovery_completed event names the offending event_ids in a validated supersedes array, and a test asserts every pre-existing comment body is byte-identical after the repair runs, including on every path where repair now refuses.

HIGH 1 resolved by a three-class problem taxonomy in replayOutcomeEvents. duplicate_event_id (the same event_id posted twice) and state_repost (the state already reached, re-recorded under a new event_id) are the two artefacts of the read-back race; retiring either leaves the ledger at exactly the state it already held, so nothing is hidden. Everything else — a skipped state, a move backward, a misused blocked/yielded pair — is classed lifecycle_violation, and repairOutcomeHistory now throws before appending anything, naming the violation and telling the operator to record the missing or corrected lifecycle event instead. It no longer drops replay.offenders[0] for an unexamined problem class.

HIGH 2 resolved in two layers. validateEvent in scripts/db-coordination-events.mjs now refuses a supersedes field on any event whose event_type is not recovery_completed, so no routine lifecycle comment can carry one at all. outcomeHistory then honours supersedes only from a recovery_completed event whose result is succeeded, and only for ids that are themselves outcome-state events of the same work issue, so neither a cross-type target nor a phantom id can suppress anything.

Deterministic event_id from (issue, state) was deliberately not implemented, for the reason recorded at generation 1. The narrower collision the review found was fixed instead: eventId now folds a sorted supersedes list into the derived material when present, so two repairs that retire different events cannot collapse onto one id. detail was deliberately NOT added, because appending it unconditionally would change the derived id of every existing event that carries one; the supersedes append is conditional and therefore has zero blast radius.

The duplicate-event_id repair no longer erases the legitimate original alongside the copy: when an id was posted more than once only the repeated occurrences are retired, so the state the repair was run to restore does not regress.
